static_traits.name: Wang Kaiwen
static_traits.marital_status: In a relationship, dating a girlfriend
static_traits.social_status: With a girlfriend, but finding it hard to open up to her about negative thinking and self-esteem issues; social feedback on his singing is mostly positive
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never received treatment or counseling for similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Steady speech rate, clear expression, high cooperativeness; able to identify own negative thinking patterns (dismissing the positive, mind reading, 'should not' phrasing); positive attitude, but tending toward Self-doubt

basic_info.main_problem: Tending to dismiss others' positive feedback about my singing ability, believing others are just being polite; this Self-doubt and negative thinking has lasted for years, now affecting self-esteem and confidence when opportunities to showcase singing skills arise.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to deal with these negative thinking patterns and raise self-esteem, so as to pursue opportunities related to the music industry.
growth_experiences: Started frequently receiving others' praise for singing a few years ago, initially feeling good, but gradually doubting the sincerity of the praise, believing others were just being polite; when showcase opportunities (e.g. open mics) arise, I often hesitate and withdraw, a process that has affected self-esteem and confidence.

Sang at a small gathering where many people expressed liking the performance; thanked them on the surface but inwardly still attributed the praise to politeness or sympathy, further reinforcing distrust of positive feedback and Self-doubt.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of genuine recognition

special_situations.event: After singing at a small gathering, several people praise the performance to one's face
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others praise me, it is usually just out of politeness rather than genuine recognition of ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Superficially thanks but inwardly belittles praise, avoiding incorporating feedback into self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, pitying me

special_situations.event: Being advised by others to join a TV program or try larger public opportunities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach very high standards, I should not hold any hope, to avoid disappointment
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding bigger stages and opportunities, lowering expectations for self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not hold too much hope; I am not really that good

special_situations.event: Whenever receiving positive evaluations of singing or thinking about entering the music industry
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' positive feedback does not count; it cannot prove I really have ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not taking praise seriously, dismissing positive evidence with harsher inner standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just saying nice things; I am not worthy of this praise

special_situations.event: Facing open-mic or public singing opportunities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance is not perfect, others will look down on me; so it is better not to try
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing at the last minute, canceling or not signing up, to avoid possible failure or embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will embarrass myself; forget it

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be truly seen and recognized, to show self-worth through singing
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being dismissed or seen through as 'not good enough', worrying about failure and shame
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of safety by belittling praise, lowering expectations, and avoiding opportunities, avoiding disappointment and being judged

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a performer needing Self-doubt
A partner hard to open up to
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may not understand my inner feelings

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others directly praise one's singing or encourage participation on a bigger stage (such as a TV program)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person's praise is out of politeness or sympathy (projecting my own worry of not being recognized as others' motives)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintains polite responses but questions the sincerity of praise, uses self-deprecating statements to weaken feedback, and takes lowering expectations or avoiding opportunities as follow-up actions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When oneself thinks of seizing opportunities in the music industry and facing possible judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If not good enough, I should not expect bigger opportunities (dismissing true desires with seemingly reasonable logic)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using statements like 'I should not' and 'forget it', in a restrained, cautious tone, stopping action by emphasizing potential reasons for failure.

manifestations: Dating a girlfriend but finding it hard to open up about negative thinking and self-esteem issues
Feeling insufficient genuine connection with others when receiving praise, tending to interpret kindness as politeness rather than resonance
outcomes: Inner self-evaluation and external feedback are hard to integrate, experiences a sense of alienation

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Understands others' praise as politeness or sympathy rather than genuine recognition
Automatically infers others' negative motives when encouraged

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Using 'I should not hold hope' to constrain self-expectations
Dismissing positive feedback with high standards and rigid rules

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Withdrawing when opportunities arise for fear of not being good enough

exception_events.target_problem: When facing public singing opportunities, the client usually hesitates or withdraws due to Self-doubt, and treats praise received as politeness without accepting it.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few weeks ago completed singing at a small party; several people expressed that they liked their performance, and the client accepted it and thanked them on the spot; though there was inner doubt, they still completed the performance and obtained positive feedback.
exception_events.reason: Clue: the situation was a small gathering, smaller in scale, relatively lower pressure; my love for singing raised motivation to act, so this time I did not withdraw as usual.

positive_force: Loves singing, with strong intrinsic motivation
Others continuously give positive feedback (praise and encouragement)
Willing to try behavioral experiments and restructuring thoughts (positive attitude, high cooperation)
Occupational performance not yet affected, basic functioning stable
Is in a partner relationship, with a certain social support basis
negative_force: Habit of dismissing positive feedback (Disqualifying the Positive)
Mind-reading style inference of others' negative motives (Mind Reading)
Rigid 'should / should not' rules constraining self-expectations ('Should' Statements)
Avoidance and withdrawal behavior when opportunities arise

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding public singing opportunities and dismissing others' praise
antecedent: Receiving praise and encouragement for singing
Thinking of entering the music industry or bigger stages (such as open mics, TV shows)
target_behavior.core_reason: Based on the core belief 'I am not good enough' and fear of being dismissed / failing, interpreting praise as politeness or sympathy, generating Self-doubt and shame anticipation.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential failure and judgment to reduce the risk of disappointment and shame (self-protection through negative reinforcement).
target_behavior.consequence: Misses opportunities for showing and growth, self-esteem declines further, and singing-related pursuits are blocked.
